correctness.rationale: For \(T_{2m+1}\) with arcs \(u\to v\) when \(v-u\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), the classes \(A=\{0,\ldots,m\}\) and \(B=\{m+1,\ldots,2m\}\) are individually transitive. Writing \(b_j=m+1+j\), the cross rule is \(a_i\to b_j\) exactly when \(i\ge j+1\); therefore the displayed interleaving is a topological order of the whole bipartite subdigraph. The triangle \(0\to m\to2m\to0\) proves one colour is impossible. An independent direct enumeration for every \(1\le m\le100\) verified the same orientation and topological-order identities.

value.rationale: The standard cyclic tournament is the canonical regular tournament in every odd order, and the strengthened acyclic dichromatic invariant is new enough that even small tournaments can require three or four colours. An exact all-order value with one explicit uniform partition is therefore a natural complete family classification despite the short proof.
